rows.claim: Controllability metrics improve held-out target ranking by >= 0.05 AUC over degree and strength, with a bootstrap CI excluding zero.
rows.evidence: 2026-06-12_cc_data.json auc_planted_hub_target: degree+strength 0.9933, full(+controllability) 0.9929; delta_auc -0.0003 with bootstrap 95% CI [-0.0019, +0.0026] (CI includes zero).
rows.scope: synthetic modular SBM (n=200, 8 modules) with 25 planted connector hubs as ground-truth target; logistic regression, 10x5 repeated CV AUC

rows.claim: Controllability carries rank information not already contained in node strength.
rows.evidence: rank_redundancy: Spearman avg-controllability ~ strength = 0.937, modal ~ strength = -0.934, avg ~ modal = -0.993; top-30 node overlap (strength vs avg-controllability) = 21/30.
rows.scope: rank space on the planted-hub substrate; controllability is near-monotone in strength so re-ranks almost nothing

rows.claim: Any incremental controllability signal reflects unique topological structure, not a degree/strength artifact.
rows.evidence: degree_preserving_null: 40 double-edge-swap rewirings with empirical weight multiset re-attached reproduce the near-zero increment (null delta mean -0.0002); observed delta lies at the 40th percentile of the null distribution.
rows.scope: synthetic degree-preserving null on the planted-hub substrate

rows.claim: On a real empirical connectome (e.g. HCP / Glasser-360) with a pre-registered behavioural or functional target, controllability carries incremental target-ranking value beyond degree and strength.
rows.evidence: not tested - all substrates are synthetic (random, modular SBM, planted hubs, dynamic-energy target); no real parcellation, no real behavioural/functional target, no pre-registered real-data ranking task.
rows.scope: would require an empirical connectome with a directed target fixed in advance; not run in this duel
